::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** May 5th 1868  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 195-6
:::

Dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd),
Thank you much for your kind answer. The second set of [cameos](cmy_books/cmybook_93.qmd) is nearly all written, but the [Monthly Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd) must have the first turn of them and that will take a good while - about a year at shortest.

I am afraid you think me very idle about the [Worthies](cmy_books/cmybook_80.qmd). The truth is that my [Mother](people/person_1606.qmd) has grown so infirm of late that I have less time than usual, and that time I thought it wise to spend in completing Monthly Packet Material, Cameos and a [story](cmy_books/cmybook_81.qmd) (of James I of Scotland in Captivity) that in case of being able to do no work, there might not be a stand still. I hope however to return ere long to Alexander the Great - whom I have left a full year on the Banks of the Granicus

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

**Note:** The first volume of *Cameos from English History* was published in 1868, the second in 1871.
